$comment: Stage 9 failure classification. The signals are named after what a transport can actually prove, not after either platform's error enum, because Swift's URLSession failure and Rust's ApiError::Network are the same event seen from two sides. The line the stage spec cares about is `burnsAttempt`: 'the link is down' and 'this page is bad' must not share a counter, or a five-hour tunnel spends every retry the one genuinely broken page needed. Three other places already make the same choice for writes — store::outbox::record_outcome's BlockedAuthentication no-op and sync::upload's Decision::Defer — and this is the read-side restatement of it.

signals.$comment: A signal is what the pass knows about one page attempt. Anything not listed here, including a future variant on either platform, is badPage by `default`: it is about this response, the page stays retryable, and treating the unknown as fatal would turn one odd server into a dead queue.
signals.ok: 200, the container walks, and the byte count matches what the mirrored manifest declared.
signals.link: The request could not be made or not finished: no route, connection refused, DNS failure, socket timeout, a body that stopped mid-stream.
signals.shortRead: A whole response arrived with fewer bytes than the manifest declared for this page. Only the declared size can tell this apart from a genuinely small image, and the manifest is the only witness that has ever been able to.
signals.corrupt: The container walk failed: bad chunk stream, missing JPEG EOI, absent GIF trailer, RIFF length that does not describe the file.
signals.tooSmall: Below the floor a real page image cannot miss by, so the response is not an image at all.
signals.writeFailed: The durable write did not complete: disk full, read-only volume, rename refused.

outcomesNote: scope decides how far the news travels. `page` marks one row and continues the book; `book` ends this book and leaves it explainable; `pass` ends the pass with no write at all; `serverQueue` ends the pass AND parks every book for that server, because the next book would fail identically and the user is paying per request.
boundsNote: maxPageAttempts is per page and per user retry. consecutiveBadPages degrades a run of badPage into a `pass`-scoped stop without burning anything more, so a dying server costs three attempts across the whole book instead of three per page (400 pages x 3). The three pass bounds exist for three different reasons and all three are needed: pages is the number the tests can state exactly, bytes is the number a 4K-page book can run away with (4 x 24 MB is a Dart `await` nobody should sit through), and elapsed is the one that keeps the pump from starving `reader_page`, which shares the process. Elapsed is checked BEFORE each page and overridden once only when zero pages have been served, so a pass always makes progress.

linkPolicy.metered: proceed only when the book's allowCellular is true; otherwise stop with linkBlocked
linkPolicy.unknown: continue a book that was already `downloading` when the pass planned it; never start a new one
linkPolicy.$comment: Android answers this from ConnectivityManager.isActiveNetworkMetered(), NOT from `transport == WIFI`: the emulator reports ETHERNET, and a transport test there would leave every download permanently blocked and look like a core bug. `unknown` is deliberately asymmetric with `metered` — refusing everything the platform cannot describe would make downloads unstartable on any device that will not answer, which is the same trap a no-op-equals-health counter fell into in Stage 8. The asymmetry is: unknown may finish work already started, may not start new work.

stopReasonsNote: stopReasons the planner can decide are in pump.json; the three runtime-only ones (badPage, badRun, paused) are produced by a pass and listed in bounds.nextInMs with how long to wait before the next one.
